attribution.note: Zitron endorses the calculation and separately expresses possibilities about fuller accounts.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the reported inputs, derived loss and hedge. Only the firm arithmetic observation is scoreable.

contract.note: The contract fairly identifies adjusted operating loss as the metric and excludes the hedged possibilities from scoring.

evidence.note: Reports the matching quarter, revenue and adjusted margin. Multiplication gives $6.954bn, rounding to $6.95bn.
Operating loss including stock compensation and net loss use different accounting measures. They do not directly establish the adjusted loss or score the hedge.
Shareholder-document reporting repeats $5.7bn revenue, but cash burn is a different metric. It does not substantiate the possibility of lower revenue.

reviews.rationale: The firm calculation is supported: $5.7bn multiplied by 122% yields about $6.95bn in adjusted operating loss. The larger losses and cash-burn figure concern different measures. The possibilities concerning fuller accounts remain unscored.

attribution.note: Zitron states the stalled-growth conclusion in his own voice.

semantics.note: The surrounding discussion supplies Q1 2026 and weekly active users as the period and measure.

contract.note: Reading stalled growth as roughly flat weekly users in the quarter discussed is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: Reports a 905m quarterly average and failure to sustain further growth after late February's 920m figure. Missing confirmed March figures limit precision.
This company disclosure supplies one February lower bound. It is consistent with the reported scale but cannot independently establish a quarterly trend.
The July milestone is outside Q1 and does not contradict a temporary stall during the target period.

reviews.rationale: The reporting supports the contract's approximate reading through the quarterly average and explicit account of growth failing to continue after February. The company disclosure is consistent but not independent trend evidence. Later growth does not refute the Q1 observation.

attribution.note: Both assessments appear as Zitron's own endorsed conclusions.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both the conversion difficulty and stalled overall growth assertions.

contract.note: Conversion difficulty does not entail that conversion is not improving. A business can improve while still struggling. The added trend requirement can determine the verdict without a speaker-supplied benchmark.

evidence.note: Supports the stalled-growth component through the quarterly average and reported failure to sustain growth after February. It supplies no conversion trend.

Company-disclosed subscriber momentum challenges the contract's stagnation assumption. Subscriber additions do not establish a conversion-rate trend; the two lower bounds also do not fix an exact paid share.
July growth is outside the target quarter and does not resolve either Q1 conversion difficulty or the Q1 stall.

reviews.rationale: The stalled-growth component has support, but the compound claim cannot fairly receive a verdict under this contract. Its conversion test adds a lack-of-improvement requirement that the speaker did not supply. Record subscriber additions neither establish conversion rates nor rule out continuing difficulty.

contract.note: The contract preserves the conditional arithmetic and correctly requires full-year results and satisfaction of the antecedent.

evidence.note: The secondary summary reports Q2 figures, not full-year results. A worsening quarterly margin does not establish the full-year antecedent or outcome.

reviews.rationale: The 2026 deadline has not passed, full-year results are unavailable and the antecedent remains unknown. Correct multiplication alone cannot resolve a forecast contract requiring realized annual figures.
